name: Cornbread-Coated Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese Wedges

ingredients.name: shredded pepper jack, Monterey jack, or cheddar cheese
pulled pork, tossed with barbecue sauce

instructions.primary_message: Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Press chilled macaroni and cheese in an even layer in the baking sheet. Sprinkle all over with jalapeño peppers and shredded cheese. With the short side of the baking sheet in front of you, layer the pulled pork evenly on half of the macaroni and cheese layer.

Using the parchment paper, fold the macaroni layer without pork over the half with pork to sandwich it. Place another baking sheet on top and press gently to condense. Transfer to the freezer and freeze until solid, at least 1 hour.
Discard parchment paper. Cut the layered macaroni and pork into squares, and then cut diagonally to create triangles. Return to freezer.

In a large cast iron skillet or wok, heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F. Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk together flour, cornmeal, sugar, salt, and baking soda. Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and add milk and eggs. Whisk together until smooth.

Remove macaroni and pork triangles from freezer. Dip a few at a time into the batter and, using a spoon, transfer them to the oil. Cook, flipping halfway, until golden brown and warmed through, 3-4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the wedges to a paper towel-lined plate. Repeat until all of the wedges have been fried. Serve warm, garnished with sliced jalapeños and barbecue sauce alongside for dipping.

description: When I have leftover mac and cheese and pulled pork after a day of barbecuing, I don't just reheat it and eat it the next day. I fold them together into these outrageous fried mac and cheese bombs, stuffed with barbecue-sauced pulled pork and coated in a cornbread crust.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 40 min.

Optional or for serving: Barbecue sauce, to serve

Notes: Any leftover mac and cheese and pulled pork will work (or you can even sub in store-bought, if you'd like), but here are some recommended recipes for the macaroni and cheese and the pulled pork. Feel free to scale this recipe up or down depending on the amount of leftovers you have.
author: Morgan Eisenberg
